## The five sections of the exam

```{=html}
<div class="exam-five">
  <div class="ef-card"><span class="ef-num">I</span><h3>Multiple Choice</h3><p>10 questions on definitions, decision rules, and trap distinctions.</p></div>
  <div class="ef-card"><span class="ef-num">II</span><h3>Bond</h3><p>One bond. Compute coupon rate, journal entry, premium/discount, interest expense, NBV, retirement.</p></div>
  <div class="ef-card"><span class="ef-num">III</span><h3>Statement of Cash Flows</h3><p>Indirect method. NI → CFO. Asset sale → CFI. Stock/debt/dividends → CFF. Reconcile to ΔCash.</p></div>
  <div class="ef-card"><span class="ef-num">IV</span><h3>Job-Order Costing</h3><p>Predetermined OH rate (estimated) · Allocated OH (predetermined × actual) · Product vs period costs.</p></div>
  <div class="ef-card"><span class="ef-num">V</span><h3>CVP Analysis</h3><p>Breakeven · Target profit · Scenario sensitivity to VC and FC changes.</p></div>
</div>
```

## Section I — Multiple Choice: 10 decision rules

Memorize these one-line answers. They cover almost every MC variant.

```{=html}
<div class="rule-stack">
<div class="rule"><strong>P/E ratio high</strong> → market expects future growth. Not current profitability.</div>
<div class="rule"><strong>Sale of PPE at loss</strong> → cash inflow = NBV − Loss. Loss adds back to NI in operating; cash goes in investing.</div>
<div class="rule"><strong>SCF basis</strong> → cash, NOT accrual. If CFO consistently lower than NI, watch for aggressive revenue recognition.</div>
<div class="rule"><strong>Direct product cost</strong> → traceable to one unit (materials, assembly labor). Indirect = factory overhead. Office salaries = period.</div>
<div class="rule"><strong>Equity vs Debt</strong> → debt holders paid first in bankruptcy. Equity = ownership + dividends. Debt = lender + interest.</div>
<div class="rule"><strong>Predetermined OH rate</strong> → uses ESTIMATED values, computed at start of year.</div>
<div class="rule"><strong>Allocated OH</strong> → predetermined rate × ACTUAL allocation base.</div>
<div class="rule"><strong>Stock split</strong> → SE unchanged. <strong>Stock repurchase</strong> → SE decreases (treasury is contra-equity, not asset).</div>
<div class="rule"><strong>Earnings management</strong> → intentional, may be within GAAP. <strong>Fraud</strong> → violates GAAP / misleads users.</div>
<div class="rule"><strong>Strong company</strong> → high ROA, high current ratio, high TIE. <strong>Dividend-investor pick</strong> → high dividend payout ratio.</div>
</div>
```

## Section II — Bond: One formula chain

```{=html}
<div class="formula-chain">
  <div class="fc-step"><span class="fc-num">1</span><div><strong>Coupon rate</strong> = Annual coupon ÷ Face value</div></div>
  <div class="fc-step"><span class="fc-num">2</span><div><strong>Issue price &gt; Face?</strong> Premium · <strong>Issue price &lt; Face?</strong> Discount · <strong>Equal?</strong> Face</div></div>
  <div class="fc-step"><span class="fc-num">3</span><div><strong>Interest expense (year 1)</strong> = Issue price × MARKET rate (NOT coupon rate)</div></div>
  <div class="fc-step"><span class="fc-num">4</span><div><strong>Amortization</strong> = Coupon (cash paid) − Interest expense</div></div>
  <div class="fc-step"><span class="fc-num">5</span><div><strong>New NBV</strong> = Old NBV − Amortization (premium) · OR + Amortization (discount)</div></div>
  <div class="fc-step"><span class="fc-num">6</span><div><strong>Retirement entry at maturity</strong> → Dr. Bonds Payable (face), Cr. Cash (face). NBV is back to face by then.</div></div>
</div>
```

::: {.fillrule}
**The decision rule that wins this section:**
**Premium** → coupon rate > market rate · total interest expense over life is **LOWER** than total coupons.
**Discount** → coupon rate < market rate · total interest expense over life is **HIGHER** than total coupons.
:::

## Section III — Statement of Cash Flows: One recipe

The indirect-method recipe. Memorize the order. Plug numbers in.

```{=html}
<div class="cfo-recipe">
<pre>
Cash Flow from Operations (Indirect Method):

      Net Income                                   ___
   +  Depreciation expense                         ___
   +  Loss on sale of PPE  (or − Gain)             ___
   ±  Changes in current operating accounts:
      − Increase in AR                             (___)
      + Decrease in AR                              ___
      + Decrease in Inventory                       ___
      − Increase in Inventory                      (___)
      − Increase in Prepaid expenses               (___)
      + Increase in AP                              ___
      + Increase in Accrued liabilities             ___
                                                  ────
   =  Cash Flow from Operations                    ___
</pre>
</div>
```

::: {.fillrule}
**The sign rule, memorize this verbatim:**
**Current ASSETS** (AR, Inventory, Prepaid) — *opposite* sign from change. Up = cash use. Down = cash source.
**Current LIABILITIES** (AP, Accrued) — *same* sign as change. Up = cash source. Down = cash use.
:::

**Then:** CFI (asset sale + asset purchase) and CFF (debt + stock + dividends). Sum the three. Should equal ΔCash on the balance sheet.

**Three quick formulas you'll need:**

```{=html}
<div class="formula-chain">
  <div class="fc-step"><span class="fc-num">A</span><div><strong>Dividends paid</strong> = Beg RE + NI − End RE</div></div>
  <div class="fc-step"><span class="fc-num">B</span><div><strong>Cash from PPE sale</strong> = NBV − Loss (or NBV + Gain). NBV = Cost − Accum Dep.</div></div>
  <div class="fc-step"><span class="fc-num">C</span><div><strong>PPE purchases</strong> from roll-forward: End PPE = Beg PPE + Purchases − Cost of PPE sold</div></div>
</div>
```

## Section IV — Job-Order Costing: One formula chain

```{=html}
<div class="formula-chain">
  <div class="fc-step"><span class="fc-num">1</span><div><strong>Predetermined OH rate</strong> = Estimated total OH ÷ Estimated allocation base (machine hours OR direct labor hours)</div></div>
  <div class="fc-step"><span class="fc-num">2</span><div><strong>Allocated OH</strong> = Predetermined OH rate × ACTUAL allocation base</div></div>
  <div class="fc-step"><span class="fc-num">3</span><div><strong>Total product cost</strong> = Direct materials + Direct labor + Allocated OH</div></div>
  <div class="fc-step"><span class="fc-num">4</span><div><strong>Period cost</strong> = Everything NOT factory-related (corporate HQ, customer service, sales, admin)</div></div>
</div>
```

::: {.fillrule}
**The decision rule that wins this section: PRODUCT vs PERIOD**

**Product** = factory-related = capitalized into inventory:
- Direct materials (DM)
- Direct labor (DL)
- Manufacturing overhead (MOH): factory rent, depreciation on factory equipment, factory supervisor, indirect materials, indirect labor

**Period** = expensed immediately:
- Corporate HQ rent
- Office admin salaries
- Sales commissions
- Customer service phone reps
- Marketing
:::

**The MOH-bucket rule:** If it's tied to the *factory*, it's MOH. If it's tied to *anything else* (corporate, sales, customer service), it's a period cost. **Direct materials and direct labor are NOT in the MOH bucket** — they get added to product cost separately.

## Section V — CVP Analysis: Two formulas

```{=html}
<div class="formula-chain">
  <div class="fc-step"><span class="fc-num">1</span><div><strong>Unit CM</strong> = Sales price per unit − Variable cost per unit</div></div>
  <div class="fc-step"><span class="fc-num">2</span><div><strong>Breakeven (units)</strong> = Fixed Costs ÷ Unit CM</div></div>
  <div class="fc-step"><span class="fc-num">3</span><div><strong>Units for target profit</strong> = (Fixed Costs + Target Profit) ÷ Unit CM</div></div>
  <div class="fc-step"><span class="fc-num">4</span><div><strong>NI at any volume</strong> = (Volume × Unit CM) − Fixed Costs</div></div>
</div>
```

::: {.fillrule}
**The scenario-handling rule:** every scenario changes one or more of: **(a)** sales price, **(b)** variable cost, **(c)** fixed cost. Always recompute unit CM and FC at the top of each scenario, then plug into the formulas. Don't use stale values.
:::

**Round up** for breakeven and target-profit unit answers. You can't sell 7,241.38 units; you need 7,242.

## What to memorize cold (10 minutes of repetition)

```{=html}
<ol class="memo-check">
  <li><strong>Bond:</strong> Premium = coupon &gt; market = lower interest expense. Discount = coupon &lt; market = higher interest expense. Interest expense = NBV × MARKET rate.</li>
  <li><strong>SCF sign rule:</strong> Current assets opposite (AR up = cash use). Current liabilities same (AP up = cash source).</li>
  <li><strong>SCF asset sale:</strong> Cash = NBV − Loss. NBV = Cost − Accum Dep. Loss adds back in CFO.</li>
  <li><strong>SCF dividends:</strong> Beg RE + NI − End RE.</li>
  <li><strong>Predetermined OH:</strong> Estimated ÷ Estimated. <strong>Allocated OH:</strong> Predetermined rate × ACTUAL.</li>
  <li><strong>Product vs period:</strong> Factory-related = product (capitalized). Everything else = period (expensed).</li>
  <li><strong>Breakeven:</strong> FC ÷ unit CM. Round UP.</li>
  <li><strong>Target profit:</strong> (FC + target) ÷ unit CM.</li>
  <li><strong>Stock split:</strong> SE unchanged. <strong>Stock repurchase:</strong> SE decreases (treasury = contra-equity).</li>
  <li><strong>P/E high</strong> = market expects growth (not current profit).</li>
</ol>
```

If you can recite all 10 in 90 seconds without looking, you have the spine. Walk in.
